- When sentiment is consistently high (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- If model shows sharp upward spike followed by high sentiment, cap the overshoot at +10% above recent 7-day average.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.33) and model forecasts rise, adjust downward by 2–5% to avoid overconfidence bias.
- If true outcome consistently lags model by 1–2 days, apply a 1-day lag correction: subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast for each lagged day.
- Mean reversion detected when model overshoots by >15% above 30-day moving average — reduce forecast by 10–15% to align with historical volatility.
- For horizon >14 days, model tends to overestimate; apply exponential decay weighting (e.g., 0.95 decay per day) to future forecasts to reduce drift.
